lines.text: Twenty-six satellites. One rocket. And a first for Starship.
On September 28th, SpaceX's Starship reached orbit for the very first time, on its fourteenth test flight.
About 275 kilometres above Earth, it released all 26 of its passengers: new Starlink V3 internet satellites.
Each V3 is designed for about one terabit per second of download capacity, roughly ten times the older version.
They're too big for SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket, so they need Starship. A full load could carry up to sixty.
Why it matters: the giant rocket just proved it can deliver real cargo to orbit.
